messages.content: write a story about a husband and wife getting ready for a short trip. one puts books in a container, and the other makes breakfast. let them check what still needs doing without one person telling the other they never help.

a husband and wife were getting ready to leave after breakfast. he put two books in a container while she made tea and bread. when he asked whether they were ready, she said there was still food on the table and cups to wash. he began to say he had already done his part, then stopped and asked what would help now. she asked him to wash the cups while she put the food away. after that, they looked around together, took the container, and left.
make the request simple.
write a story about two people getting ready for a short trip. one puts books in a container, and the other makes breakfast. they ask what still needs to be done.
can doing one part mean nobody should ask for help with the rest?

not always. finishing one part says what is done, but the whole plan may still need work. in this story, they can talk about what is left instead of making help a question about who is always good or wrong.
write a short conversation where they check what is left.
the books are ready. what is still left? the cups need washing, and the food needs to go away. i can wash while you put the food away. then let us check once more before leaving.
give the check simply.
the books are ready. what else needs doing before we leave? could you wash the cups while i put the food away? yes, then we can check together.
now give the end without adding another task.
they took the container of books, checked that they had the key, and left for the trip.
i want to write about a plant without saying its specific kind. can the words still make a clear picture?
yes. you can say where it is, how large it is, what color the leaves are, and what people do near it. the general word plant can keep those details.
answer simply.
you can use plant and still give clear details. for example: a small plant with green leaves stands near the window in a white container.
now make it a different plant, large enough to stand on the floor.
a large plant with green leaves stands on the floor near the window in a white container.
does that tell you the container was large too?
you have not given the container size. if you need that detail in the story, say whether the container is large or small.
make it simple.
you have not given the container size. you can add that detail if it is important.
now it is a large white container. write one sentence.
a large plant with green leaves stands in a large white container on the floor near the window.
if i change the container to blue, keep the leaves green.
a large plant with green leaves stands in a large blue container on the floor near the window.
my uncle wrote a note for my aunt. my sister read it to me over the phone. if i say my sister told me the message, does that make her the person who wrote it?
no. your sister gave the words to you, but your uncle wrote the note. telling someone a message and writing the original words are different parts.
answer simply.
your uncle wrote the note. your sister read it to you, so you heard it from her.
what if i want to tell my mother where i got the information?
you can say: my sister read me a note that my uncle wrote for my aunt. that keeps the people and their parts clear.
now ask who the note was for without choosing the wrong person.
who was the note for?
my aunt. does hearing it mean i should do every task in it?
not just from hearing it. the note was for your aunt. you would need to know whether any part was also for you before taking it as your own task.
answer simply.
not just because you heard it. the note was for your aunt, and you have not said any part was a request for you.
now make a short question i can ask my aunt about helping.
would you like help with anything in the note, or is it something you want to do yourself?
if i say my friend seems tired, does that mean they told me they are tired?
not from that alone. seems can be about what you think from seeing or hearing them. it is different from saying they told you. you can ask rather than call the feeling known.
say it simply.
you think they may be tired, but they have not told you that in the words you gave. you can ask how they feel.
what would be a kind question?
would you like some quiet, or are you feeling okay to keep talking?
i do not want to give two choices if they feel something else.
then ask: how are you feeling right now? that leaves room for their own answer rather than making tired the only possible feeling.
keep the question alone.
how are you feeling right now?
now they say they are not tired, just thinking about something. what should you use?
use their answer. they said they are thinking about something, not feeling tired. keep what they said clear rather than changing it to your first idea.
answer simply.
they told you they are thinking, not tired. keep that clear instead of choosing tired from how they looked.
i use a tool from my brother. it was on his shelf before i took it. when i finish, i give it back into his hands. can i say it is on the shelf again?
not from that alone. you returned the tool to your brother, but you did not say he put it back on the shelf. the last place you gave is in his hands.
now he puts it in a container under his desk. what changed?
the tool moved from his hands to the container under his desk. it is still his tool in the example.
if i look on the shelf tomorrow and do not see it, can i say it is lost?
not just from the old shelf being empty. you know he put it under the desk later. check that place or ask him before saying it is lost.
make that simple.
it may still be in the container under his desk. the shelf is only the old place, so not finding it there does not mean the tool is lost.
write a short question i can ask before i use it again.
may i use your tool again, and is it still in the container under your desk?
why ask where if i remember where he put it?
because it may have moved after that. you know an old place, but asking can help you know whether that information is still right.
say it simply.
you know where he put it before, but it may have moved later. asking can help you know where it is now.
six children are reading in one room. two leave the room and wait by the door. can i say they left the school?
no. you only said they left the room and waited by the door. the door may still be inside the school. leaving one room is not the same as leaving the whole building.
use children in a simple answer.
six children were in a room. two went out and waited near the door. you have not said they left the school.
how many children are still in the room if nothing else changed?
four children are still in the room, and two are near the door.
now one of the two comes back in. how many are in the room then?
five are in the room, and one is still near the door.
does comes back tell you the one by the door went home?
no. you have not said that child moved away. coming back is about one child, not a new fact about the other one.
now i say the last child comes back too. write one sentence with all six.
all six children are back in the room.
can that be true even if they do not all sit down to read again?
yes. being back in the room gives their place. it does not by itself say what every child starts doing next.
i want to say the book that my aunt gave me is on the table. can you make it shorter without changing who gave the book or who got it?
the book from my aunt is on the table.
keep my first idea simple.
my aunt gave me the book, and it is on the table. make that shorter without changing the people.
now i say the book i gave my aunt is on the table. does that give the same person as the one who gave the book?
no. now you are the person who gave the book, and your aunt is the person who got it. that is different from your aunt giving a book to you.
answer simply.
no. one sentence has your aunt giving you a book. the other has you giving your aunt a book.
what if it is the same book going from one person to the other and back?
then both could be about that book at different parts of the story, but you would need to explain the order. the short sentence alone does not give that whole story.
make it one simple story.
my aunt gave me a book. later, i gave the same book back to her. both parts are about one book, but the person giving it changed.
now ask whose book is on the table now without choosing the answer.
whose book is on the table now?
picoboi, write this as a message i can send: i would like to visit my sister after work tomorrow. ask whether that is good for her.
would it be okay if i visited you after work tomorrow?
why did you not say my sister in the message?
you are sending it to your sister, so you can speak to her as you. outside the message, i can say you want to visit your sister.
now tell me what i want to do, not words to send.
you would like to visit your sister after work tomorrow.
ask my last request simply.
tell me what i want to do, rather than writing words to send.
now does using i in the first message mean you have a sister?
no. i in that message is the person who will send it, which is you. it is not new information about my family.
can you keep that clear if i ask you who wants the visit?
you want to visit your sister. i was helping write the message for you.
now give just the message again, no explanation.
would it be okay if i visited you after work tomorrow?
